flags: minor: overlaps with R017-07 (both interpret Albescu's behavior in paragraph 5); item 07's 'calm under pressure' reading and this item's 'confidence' reading reinforce each other
R017-01.notes: Sending the critic's ticket to the narrator and leaving a knife with no note are wordless signals of trust. A (testing for failure) is the main trap but the knife gift contradicts it; C and D are unsupported.

R017-02.notes: The cooks' Lyon theory is offered as a possible reason, and 'Whether that was true, no one knew.' B ('real reason') is the trap for readers who skip that qualification; C overstates detail; D is unsupported (it is the narrator, not the cooks, who is said to resent her).

flags: minor: tests the same phrase ('read her silence') as R017-06, so each item cues the other ('interpret' / 'looked for any sign')
R017-03.notes: Trying to read her silence shows the narrator wanted her approval. A takes the phrase literally, and B and C contradict paragraphs 2 and 3.

flags: minor: 'little public recognition' is a slightly soft fit, since the lamb was praised, though only in one sentence; still the only defensible choice
R017-04.notes: The lamb got a single sentence of praise while the dessert, which the narrator did not make, got three paragraphs, so the narrator's work received little public notice (a contrast with Albescu's private recognition). A contradicts the praise; B and D are unsupported.

flags: minor: the key closely paraphrases the passage sentence ('the host recognized him')
minor: same phrase as R017-03, so the two items cue each other
R017-06.notes: To 'read' silence means to interpret it. C ('study') is a weak near-miss.

R017-07.notes: While others panic, she doesn't look up and finishes plating, which shows composure. A ('indifferent') is a trap based on 'didn't look up', but routing the ticket deliberately shows she cares. B and C are contradicted.

flags: minor: the memory gap could also be read as nerves; C's 'intense and absorbing' covers that broadly enough to remain the single best answer
R017-08.notes: A blank memory of a high-stakes moment conveys its intensity. B is the trap (he had cooked it often, but 'no longer mattered' is wrong); A and D are unsupported.

R017-09.notes: 'the one I had made every night for six weeks.' B (four months) and C (three months) are traps drawn from other time references in the passage.
